clue.text: Hold faith to convey confidence

parts.note: to carry something is to hold it
a conviction is a firmly held belief, a faith

explanation.surface: Keeping your beliefs is a way of seeming self-assured to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that carries conviction is persuasive, so it sounds sure of itself to listeners.

clue.text: Work left prematurely to go to bed too soon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: quitting your career before the usual age

definitions.text: to go to bed too soon
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: retiring for the night at an early hour

explanation.surface: Someone clocks off from the job early and then turns in for the night too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: To retire can mean both to stop working and to go to bed, so the phrase covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement is stopping work for good, and retiring is also an old-fashioned way of saying heading off to sleep.

clue.text: Ways to go to get instructions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: routes or bearings one might head in
second meaning: guidance on how to do something

explanation.surface: A traveller asks which routes will lead somewhere they can be told what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions are both compass bearings or routes and a set of orders explaining how to proceed.

clue.text: Progress with publicity at front of church

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
the van is the front of an army or procession, as in vanguard
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church campaign grows with posters put up at its entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to move forward, which is what progress means as a verb or noun.

clue.text: Assist sailor with alien

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
ET is the film extra-terrestrial, an alien

explanation.surface: A seaman is asked to help out along with a creature from space.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help, though usually in some wrongdoing, as in aid and abet.

clue.text: Legal document is union's authorisation

parts.note: a marriage is a union; the possessive makes it describe the next word
a licence is an authorisation, formal permission

explanation.surface: A legal paper turns out to be the permission a wedding needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage licence is an official certificate permitting a couple to wed, so it is a legal paper.

clue.text: Coke drunken lady spilled is out of harm's way

indicators.note: something spilled is scattered about, so the letters before it land in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman knocks over her cola, but the drink is safely away from danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'spilled' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept under lock and key is secured, safely protected from harm or theft.

clue.text: Paid regularly to raid seal compound

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters before it are mixed together afresh

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Commandos earn a steady wage for storming an enclosure where seals are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaried worker receives a fixed sum at regular intervals rather than hourly wages.

clue.text: By going without water becomes very clever

indicators.note: going without here means wrapping round the outside of the next word

parts.note: taken as written
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone claims that abstaining from drinking water makes you a genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going without' reads as doing without, but it means placed outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainy is an informal word for highly intelligent.

clue.text: Cook's point for grating

parts.note: to grill is to cook; the 's stands for has, joining it to what follows
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A chef's spike is used for shredding cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like a cooking verb in this kitchen setting, but it is a noun: a metal lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grid of bars over an opening, the same thing as a grating.

clue.text: No treaty made up for the lawyer

indicators.note: made up means invented or put together, so the letters are assembled in a fresh order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: With no agreement drafted, someone blames the legal counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a lawyer, the usual American word for one.

clue.text: Mark some, discarding others

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is kept, with the rest thrown away

parts.note: sits in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A teacher grades a few papers and throws the rest away.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as: take some of 'discarding', throwing out the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Plan with supporter in order to achieve set aims

definitions.text: in order to achieve set aims

parts.note: a tactic is a plan or scheme
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: Someone schemes alongside a backer to reach their goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting tactically means choosing moves for a specific purpose, with particular goals in view.

clue.text: Bungling of clumsy one spoiled duet

parts.note: inept means clumsy or unskilled

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so the following word's letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An awkward singer ruins a two-part song through sheer incompetence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptitude is a lack of skill, so bungling as a noun is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Count in trouble for smarminess

indicators.note: being in trouble means being in a mess, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An aristocrat lands in hot water for being too oily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of 'in trouble', but it belongs to the fodder alongside 'Count'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction can mean an excessively ingratiating, oily manner, which is smarminess.

clue.text: Resistance of French at barrier

parts.note: de is French for of
a fence is a barrier

explanation.surface: The French Resistance makes a stand at a barricade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance of French' suggests the wartime French Resistance, but only 'Resistance' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence is the act of resisting attack, so it is a form of resistance.

clue.text: Entertaining Japanese women with cheery sound son has made

indicators.note: sound tells us to use the way a word is said rather than its spelling

parts.note: gay in its old sense of cheery, spelt as the start of the Japanese word
S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful noise from a boy accompanies a group of Japanese hostesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Japanese word is pronounced 'gay-sha', so its first syllable is a sound-alike of the old word for cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Geishas are Japanese women trained to entertain guests with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: Police officer's esteem for nerve

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with the 's added
respect is esteem

explanation.surface: A detective admires someone for their courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nerve' reads as courage in the surface, but here it is cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve can mean impudent cheek, and disrespect is that kind of rudeness.

clue.text: One member, a Maltese, initially becomes a religious leader

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is short for member, as in MP
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A member of a Maltese congregation rises to lead its worship.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, so he is a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Incentive for a call to action

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a prompt that provokes a response

explanation.surface: A bonus is offered to rouse people into doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus is anything that spurs activity, whether a reward or a prompt that triggers a reaction.

clue.text: Related when Communist left for dead

indicators.note: left here means departed, so those letters go missing from the word

parts.note: taken as written
a Red is a Communist

explanation.surface: A tale was told after a Communist was abandoned to die.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters to remove are scattered: the R and E at the front and the D at the end of 'Related'.
explanation.definitionFit: Late is used of someone who has died, as in the late king.

clue.text: In style for current year

parts.note: a trend is a current, a prevailing direction
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Something is fashionable just for this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective meaning present-day, but it is a noun: a drift or tendency.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, which is being in style.

clue.text: Good French material for a hat

parts.note: bon is French for good
net is a mesh fabric

explanation.surface: Fine French cloth is chosen to make a piece of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a hat tied under the chin, the classic baby's or Easter style.

clue.text: Did cadet somehow become hooked?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way than shown

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A worried question about whether a young recruit fell into a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooked is the informal word for being dependent on a drug or habit, which is being addicted.
